claim_text: Workday's customer notice: its disaster-recovery site unexpectedly connected to production databases
summary: Workday's notice to customers, quoted by two universities, said its disaster-recovery site unexpectedly connected to production databases and left data inconsistent.
detail: Workday then put all WD1 production tenants into maintenance and promised updates every 30 minutes. This confirms what Workday told customers, not an independent finding. Workday has not published a root-cause report or said how the DR site reached production. Press accounts call it a backup test; Workday's wording is a weekly maintenance-window validation, and DRJ says it was not the formal semiannual DR test.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Washington University's status page quotes Workday's notice word for word and Florida Atlantic's notice relays the same disaster-recovery and inconsistent-data account; two universities posted it independently.

claim_text: Workday said the outage was not related to a cybersecurity incident
summary: Workday said the outage was not a cybersecurity or security incident: a spokesperson told WUSA9 on Saturday, Nov 14, and the company told USA TODAY the same in a Nov 18 report.
detail: USA TODAY also reports Workday saying there is no indication the outage is connected to other recent outages. Two independent outlets each got this from Workday, so it is Confirmed that Workday said it. It is the company's own denial, not an independent finding: no regulator, CISA or outside researcher has confirmed or contradicted it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: WUSA9 (TEGNA) quotes the Workday spokesperson and USA TODAY (Gannett) says Workday confirmed it to the paper: two outlets with their own sourcing. UC Today repeats the WUSA9 statement.

claim_text: Workday acknowledged a service disruption on Friday, Nov 13, and users saw 'Workday is currently unavailable'
summary: On Friday afternoon, Nov 13, Workday told KRON4 some customers were experiencing a service disruption and it was working urgently to resolve it; users saw a 'Workday is currently unavailable' page.
detail: KRON4 reported more than 2,900 Downdetector reports as of 3:15 PM that day. Workday did not name affected customers or say how many were affected.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Workday's own maintenance page shows the unavailable message, and KRON4 and Just The News each quote the same Workday statement acknowledging the disruption.

claim_text: Employees at affected organizations could not clock in, see pay, request time off or file for benefits
summary: Employees at affected employers could not clock in and out, view pay information, request time off or file for benefits while the platform was unavailable.
detail: Emerson College extended its open enrollment deadline to noon ET on Monday, Nov 16 because staff could not log in, per Edit USA; other employers posted their own notices. Check your employer's notice for deadlines.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three outlets report the same effects; Edit USA also relays a university deadline extension that shows the effect on real employees.

claim_text: Workday serves about 11,500 organizations; it has not said how many were affected
summary: Workday serves about 11,500 organizations worldwide, per WUSA9; neither Workday nor any outlet says how many were affected.
detail: Headlines such as 'millions of employees' (Engadget) are an outlet's estimate. They are not a Workday figure, and the 11,500 is Workday's total customer count.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: WUSA9 gives the customer count and says it was not clear how many were affected; Engadget's headline figure of 'millions' is not sourced to Workday.

claim_text: Workday said service was restored by 11 AM ET on Saturday, Nov 14; some customers came back at other times
summary: Workday said service was restored by 11 AM ET on Saturday, Nov 14, with two data centers affected. Florida Atlantic reported production back at 10:30 AM ET; Washington University marked its outage resolved at 6:49 PM CST.
detail: Workday told customers the weekly service update and reindexing would finish for most customers by 11 AM ET, with later tenants notified individually. USC reported about 60 percent of tenants released early Saturday. Employers posted restoration at different times.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Workday's spokesperson statement in WUSA9 matches the Florida Atlantic, USC and Washington University notices, each posted independently by those institutions.

claim_text: The White House said on Nov 18 it sees no indication of a cyberattack behind the recent tech outages; it did not name Workday
summary: A Nov 18 White House release quotes the DNI and the National Security Adviser seeing no indication of a coordinated cyberattack behind recent tech outages, and no evidence the incidents are related.
detail: The release names the FAA, Microsoft and the banks. It does not mention Workday, so it is context, not a finding about Workday. This confirms what the officials said, not an independent finding.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The White House release is the primary document and carries the quotes.

claim_text: Al Jazeera lists Workday among the outages of the past week; a former FEMA head urged caution about first answers
summary: On Nov 20 Al Jazeera listed Workday among the recent US outages and quoted a former FEMA head saying first answers should not be taken as absolute while causes are checked.
detail: The article does not say Workday's outage was a hack and does not add any Workday facts. It reports US officials downplaying a link between the incidents.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The article names Workday among the week's outages and relays the expert's caution.

claim_text: Disaster Recovery Journal: none of five outages in four days was a cyberattack, and Workday's DR environment triggered its outage
summary: A Nov 16 trade-press analysis says none of the five outages, Workday's included, was a cyberattack, and that Workday's own disaster-recovery environment triggered its disruption.
detail: It is one outlet's analysis built on Workday's public notices and press reports; it adds no new primary evidence. It says all five root causes are still preliminary and that Workday has not explained why its DR services reached production.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The analysis restates Workday's notice and says the root cause is still preliminary.

claim_text: Forum posts claimed the DR site first connected to production hours earlier and that one environment was involved first
summary: A vendor blog repeating forum posts says people claimed the disaster-recovery site connected to production hours before the outage and that only one environment (WD5) was involved at first.
detail: The blog itself calls these claims unverified and does not rely on them. No Workday notice or outlet supports them. Shown as a rumor; never as fact.
label: Rumor
why_it_supports: The blog says the forum claims are unverified; no primary source backs them.

claim_text: Social-media monitoring data shared with Axios: suspected bots wrote about a third of the conspiracy posts during the Workday outage
summary: A Nov 19 Axios report, citing data from the monitoring firm PeakMetrics, says suspected bots accounted for 34% of conspiracy-related posts during Friday's Workday outage, compared with 27% of other posts.
detail: Axios says there is no publicly established evidence that the week's outages were part of a coordinated cyberattack. This is about who spread the hack theories online, not about what caused the outage, and it is one firm's classification relayed by one outlet.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Axios gives the Workday-specific figures from the PeakMetrics analysis and states that no public evidence shows a coordinated cyberattack.
